dedupe_keys.name: unpacking the cape town drought lessons learned african centre for cities 2019

description: This climate resilience paper by Gina Ziervogel, commissioned by South Africa's Cities Support Programme in the National Treasury, reflects on how Cape Town responded to the 2017 to 2018 drought and what other cities can learn. It describes three phases of response, a new normal in February to September 2017, demand management and Day Zero from October 2017 to February 2018, and drought recovery from March 2018, and notes that seven of South Africa's eight metros imposed restrictions in the 2016 to 2017 summer. The lessons cover governance across city, provincial and national levels, data, expertise and communication, a systems view of supply including groundwater and financing, and building adaptive capacity by defining a water sensitive city and integrating climate change into planning, with an appendix of barriers and enablers. Coverage: one city, focused on governance. Access: a free PDF; the licence is not stated. Caveats: a qualitative reflection, and the paper says only some aspects are examined in depth. It supports drought adaptation policy analysis, and relates to the Frontiers in Water analysis of the same crisis in the catalogue.
